title: The Sabbath Year and Jubilee

questions.question: What happened to the land every seventh year?
options: It had a Sabbath of solemn rest
questions.correctAnswer: It had a Sabbath of solemn rest
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:4 (ESV): "But in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of solemn rest for the land, a Sabbath to the Lord."

questions.question: How often was the Year of Jubilee?
options: Every 50th year (after seven weeks of years)
questions.correctAnswer: Every 50th year (after seven weeks of years)
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:10 (ESV): "And you shall consecrate the fiftieth year... It shall be a jubilee for you."

questions.question: What was proclaimed throughout the land in the Jubilee?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:10 (ESV): "Proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants."

questions.question: What happened to property and possessions in the Jubilee?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:10 (ESV): "Each of you shall return to his property and each of you shall return to his clan."

questions.question: Were they allowed to sow or reap during the Jubilee?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:11 (ESV): "You shall neither sow nor reap what grows of itself nor gather the grapes..."

questions.question: What sound announced the Jubilee?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:9 (ESV): "Then you shall sound the loud trumpet... throughout all your land."

questions.question: On what specific day was the Jubilee trumpet sounded?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:9 (ESV): "On the Day of Atonement you shall sound the trumpet."

questions.question: How were they to eat if they didn't plant in the seventh year?
options: The land will yield fruit for them to eat
questions.correctAnswer: The land will yield fruit for them to eat
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:21 (ESV): "I will command my blessing on you in the sixth year, so that it will produce a crop sufficient for three years."

questions.question: If a brother becomes poor and sells himself, how should he be treated?
options: As a hired worker and sojourner
questions.correctAnswer: As a hired worker and sojourner
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:39-40 (ESV): "You shall not make him serve as a slave: as a hired worker and a sojourner he shall be with you."

questions.question: What about charging interest to a poor brother?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:36 (ESV): "Take no interest from him or profit, but fear your God."

questions.question: Who is the ultimate owner of the land?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:23 (ESV): "The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is mine."

questions.question: What is the "redemption" of land?
options: Buying it back by a kinsman
questions.correctAnswer: Buying it back by a kinsman
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:25 (ESV): "Then his nearest kinsman shall come and redeem what his brother has sold."

questions.question: Did the law of Jubilee listed here apply to houses in walled cities?
options: No, they could be redeemed only within a year, then became permanent
questions.correctAnswer: No, they could be redeemed only within a year, then became permanent
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:29-30 (ESV): "If it is not redeemed within a full year, then the house... shall belong in perpetuity to him who bought it; it does not go out in the Jubilee."

questions.question: Levitical cities were an exception to the walled city rule. How?
options: The Levites may redeem their houses at any time
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites may redeem their houses at any time
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:32 (ESV): "The Levites may redeem at any time the houses in the cities they possess."

questions.question: From whom could the Israelites take slaves?
options: The nations that are around you
questions.correctAnswer: The nations that are around you
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:44 (ESV): "As for your male and female slaves... you may buy male and female slaves from among the nations that are around you."

key_verse_text: And you shall consecrate the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you...
